title: The Secret Superpower of World Cup Songs (It's Not Just Soccer!)
summary: Have you ever heard a song so exciting it made you want to jump up and dance—even if you weren't watching a game? That's the magic of World Cup songs! These aren't just background music; they're like a giant, global high-five. Some have even changed people's lives. Take Shakira's 'Waka Waka (This Time for Africa)' from 2010. It mixed African and Colombian beats and was absolutely everywhere. You couldn't escape it—and honestly, nobody wanted to! It became the most streamed World Cup song ever and even earned a Guinness World Record. But here's the coolest part: while making the video, Shakira met a soccer player named Gerard Piqué. They later had two kids! 'It turned me into my mother,' she said. How wild is that? But the story of World Cup music starts way earlier. Back in 1962, a Chilean rock band called Los Ramblers made a peppy song to cheer for their team. FIFA didn't even ask them to! It became a huge hit, and that's when the big bosses realized: people love a sports soundtrack. Since then, we've gotten all kinds of bops. In 2006, opera singers Il Divo and R&B star Toni Braxton made a beautiful ballad about 'the glory and the pain' of the game. In 2014, Pitbull and Jennifer Lopez gave us a club banger that felt more like a dance party than a soccer match. And in 2022, 'Hayya Hayya' (which means 'let's go' in Arabic) blended Afrobeat and Middle Eastern sounds with singers from America, Nigeria, and Qatar. Each song is a little time capsule of sound and joy. So as the 2026 games kick off, maybe give these anthems a listen. You might just find your new favorite pump-up jam!
why_it_matters: Even if you don’t play soccer, a powerful song can make you feel connected to a worldwide celebration, just like when your school’s favorite song brings everyone together.

background_read: The FIFA World Cup is the biggest soccer tournament in the world, held every four years by an organization called FIFA.
The first famous World Cup song was made by a band in Chile in 1962, and since then, official and unofficial songs have hyped up fans.
The 2026 World Cup will take place in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, so new anthems are on the way.

WHAT: World Cup songs are more than just background music; they became global anthems and a 'time capsule of sound and joy.'
WHERE: At World Cup tournaments across the globe, from 1962 until the upcoming 2026 event.
